item.title: Israel ‘officially sanctions’ torture of Palestinian prisoners to extract confessions, report concludes
item.description: Public Committee Against Torture in Israel examined 42 complaints against Shin Bet interrogators over past decade Israel has institutionalised the use of torture to extract confessions from Palestinian prisoners, sometimes documenting abuse in official records or granting advanced approval for “special measures” in interrogation, according to a report from the Public Committee Against Torture in Israel (PCATI). item.description: Madrid correspondent Sam Jones and European community affairs correspondent Ashifa Kassam report on a pivotal election in Spain this weekend, which could see longtime PM Pedro Sánchez replaced by a conservative coalition including the far right He has become an icon of the European left. item.title: Las incógnitas del 7 de octubre: Israel busca crear una posible comisión de investigación
item.description: La posible creación de una comisión de investigación sobre los ataques del 7 de octubre de 2023 marca un giro en la política israelí. Tras años de resistencia por parte de Benjamin Netanyahu, el Parlamento dio un primer paso para esclarecer los hechos que precedieron al ataque de Hamás y la guerra en Gaza. item.title: Trouble for Netanyahu? Israeli judges question key charges in corruption trial
item.description: Judges in the long-running corruption trial of Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu handed his defence a major boost on Wednesday in recommending the prosecution drop one of the cases in which he is accused of bribery. The recommendations, which came as Israel's longest-serving prime minister fights for his political survival, were immediately cheered by Netanyahu's right-wing allies who demanded the trial be brought to an end.
